Why isn't the length 4 here?

The protocol uses the last two octets of the IP as a Hardware ID, and this message type seems to put the first two octets of the console's IP in a slightly different spot.  I wanted to show where we are getting the IP address from.
See Source 1 in packet number 7 of [this pcap](https://gitlab.com/-/project/7898047/uploads/980c5e5858e1aebd33874956522c7e44/livewire_test_pcap_anon.pcapng)

Ah, I was thinking you were selecting the bytes + value (like adding with proto_tree_add_item(), but you are  showing the range of bytes that appear to hold the 4  bytes that comprise the IP address..
The capture doesn't have a TCP example, but what is the actual minimal length you would need before you could possibly work out what the length is?  Isn't it \> 1 ?

I haven't seen it, but I don't think anything would prevent just sending a `\n`.

Here's a pcap with some TCP and UDP LWCP traffic.

[lwcp_tcp_filtered.pcapng](/uploads/22e8fff0f9b7652e10319581ef62b430/lwcp_tcp_filtered.pcapng)

If we start with the delimiter, it's going to have a length of just 1. It's not going to be a valid frame anyway, so I'm not sure what would go here that's not arbitrary.  We're just searching for a newline as a delimiter, and the length is whatever is up to the delimiter.

Honestly, I don't understand the LWCP protocol, and how you know when a PDU ends.   I think the frames reassembled into frame 14 are probably mostly separate commands/events/reports, and in frame 14 you only break down the first of these segments (i.e., the data from frame 2), and ignore the rest.

They all end in \\r\\n, and they don't go into quotes or encapsulations, so I'm not sure why it's not treating each one as a separate PDU.  They all have the PSH bit set (usually a very good indication the they end a PDU), but is this just a synthetic test file that you created maybe?
Oh, I broke something here.  That was previously decoding as separate LWCP messages.  Stand by.
OK. I think that fixed it.  I probably made an error earlier today and replaced a `FALSE` with a `true`!

That looks better.

Is the text inside the Encap in frame 14 XML (though not a full document) ?  I wondered about sending it to the XML dissector?  As usual, the best way to view text-based protocols is probably in Follow | TCP stream...

It looks like XML but I can't say for sure it'll always be XML.  The only time I've seen the encapsulation was in this instance.  I may have some work to do there because the LWCP protocol has properties and values for "SET" and "INDI" operations, so I probably want to split them out in the future.
You are intentionally creating a -ve unsigned number?  Is that defined behaviour?

The PSID in the advertisements is unsigned, so that's why in the `source_info_t` struct it's unsigned.  When dealing with a backfeed (from the console back to the source), it has the same PSID but I need to store its information separately, so that's why I negate it and cast it.  I could do the same by flipping a bit, if that's nicer.  It's just so it has a different key in the tree, so when we refer to that source, we can fetch the correct name, etc.
I'm honestly not sure, if it works for you we can leave it for now (unless someone else wades in).
